records.subject: Getting started with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Zara,

Thanks for setting up Vantage Partners on Wrenfield. If your team is more than one person, inviting them now tends to pay off -- Wrenfield is built around teammates working on shared tasks, not solo lists.

Let me know how the first week goes.

Cheers,
Priya Chen

decisions.rationale: 6 days in, no project, no invite, no key milestone, zero tickets, and no customer reply to either outreach (email:7a13baeb, email:f13a14ee) despite a held onboarding call (calendar:babc20bd). Team plan plus engaged call attendance gives some chance of self-start in the remaining 8 days, but total silence post-call points low.

draft.subject: Your first project in Wrenfield
draft.body:
Hi Zara,

Thanks again for the onboarding call last week. Since then I haven't wanted to pile on emails, so just one practical thought: projects are the main organizing unit in Wrenfield, and tasks live inside them, so getting a first project up is usually the step that makes everything else click. The in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project, and a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Would a 15-minute call this week help? I'm happy to work through that first project with you live.

Best,
Priya
